newsitem.title: USA: High U.S. gasoline imports may dent price rally.
newsitem.headline: High U.S. gasoline imports may dent price rally.

text.p: Forecasts for a U.S. gasoline rally in the coming weeks may be dented by expectations for 650,000 barrels per day (bpd) of gasoline imports in February, according to traders.
"We're basically sucking gasoline from all over the globe," according to one market player. "It's not an armada. Basically we've got the Seventh Fleet of gasoline this month."
But other players were quick to note that the high volumes of imports correlated strongly with what many considered a high level of refinery maintenance this winter.
"I'm detecting it's a higher than average level of imports, but what's tempering that is the maintenance that's going on," said another trader.

According to some estimates, gasoline imports to the U.S. are expected to total 18.142 million barrels for February based on expectations of 56 cargoes scheduled to arrive. This translates into an historically high 647,000 bpd.
One player said the imports, coupled with the return of some U.S. refining units that entered maintenance in January, should quash any bullish moves in gasoline prices.
Some bullish traders said a seasonal upward move in gasoline prices is probably unavoidable, but may be tempered if imports remain high for an extended period.

"I think the run-up is going to happen anyway, but if we come out of the turnarounds and the import levels remain high, then that might put a cap on how significant the rally would be," the second trader said.

Many of the ships headed to the U.S. are much larger than 30,000 to 35,000 tonne cargoes that usually arrive, according to one trader in Houston, with at least 12 ships said to be carrying cargoes of 60,000 tonnes or larger due to the economic advantage of moving those amounts.

The large amount of imports could boost U.S. gasoline inventories by more than 9 million barrels by the end of February, according to the trader, based on average daily demand of about 7.55 million bpd.
But those figures may be complicated by the fact that many of the cargoes are not finished gasoline and will require additional blending before hitting the market.
The American Petroleum Institute put U.S. gasoline stocks at 201.297 million barrels for the week ended Janaury 24, about 11.001 million barrels below the corresponding year-ago figure.
